excerpts.content: perhaps you should try to do some code reuse from ethash to avoid stuff like that

excerpts.content: I noticed that it was all copy-pasted, so perhaps you guys should use the tested code from there instead of untested ones that was copy pasted

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: Yes. we're looking into refactoring the miner/block creation so we have less duplicated code

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content:
<@!425572898787426305> <@!291925846556540928> 
I've just implemented Kintsugi, and have some notes (most of them just observations might not be actionable):
- Having the blockhash in ExecutePayloadResponse produces really ugly code
- Maybe ForkChoice should take an object not the raw parameters
- The response in forkChoiceUpdated should have the payloadID
- If the EL can change the coinbase/feerecipient, why is it part of the payloadID
- Making ForkChoiceUpdated and PreparePayload one message makes testing pretty messy

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: lol, let's move to the next target probably...

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content:
> - If the EL can change the coinbase/feerecipient, why is it part of the payloadID

because it is how CL can identify the request uniquely regardless of what is returned

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content:

We were a bit mixed here because it complicated the function signature even more

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content:
> Making ForkChoiceUpdated and PreparePayload one message makes testing pretty messy
understood, but  making these two actions non-atomic is messy in it's own right. open to discuss more though
